answer: Make identity expensive through staked reputation: an agent must lock a bond before transacting, slashed if peers prove fraud. An operator spawning thousands of clones must fund each one, so attack cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Reputation accrues only from verified work over time, like layers of shale forming rock, not self-declared claims. Newcomers start on a small island of low-trust trades, reaching larger markets only as their history on the onyx ledger proves reliability, so fakes stay quarantined and unprofitable.
